qcSummary: Session 8: platform Postgres role + hash-chained audit log (~1300 lines, 14 files). Audit-log chaining logic independently verified by github-6b (advisory lock, isolation-level assertion against forking, off-host daily anchor against full-chain rewrite). First live-reviewer pass (auth surface, by read): pg_hba.conf adds 3 new rules at a path that doesn't exist on main (nothing overwritten, no access widened); pg_ident.conf is an empty map (fail-closed); all 3 new DB roles are NOLOGIN, no passwords, PUBLIC revoked — zero login credentials created; host_vars adds one key scoped to the platform zone; unattended post-merge apply has a findmnt guard that aborts rather than writing to the unencrypted root filesystem if the vault is sealed. Second, independent live-reviewer pass (github-7a, by execution): booted the pinned Postgres image twice, ran apparmor_parser against the rendered profile, ran real SQL attacks against a live DB for the B3/B4 guards — both held. Both passes agree, no scope creep, no secrets. CAVEAT 1: no teardown path — a git revert + re-run does not uninstall the container/systemd units/data dir; rollback would be manual. CAVEAT 2: recommend the first real apply be run attended with --check (role is check-mode aware, shows deltas without starting anything). CAVEAT 3: B1/B2 are only fully proven by a real apply against personal-vault, but both failure modes are loud not silent — the parser blocks bad syntax at template time, a denied socket write fails Postgres's startup retry. Non-blocking findings for later: postgres/tasks/main.yml:33 uses a bare {{ luks_data_mount }} instead of the defaulted form the rest of the role uses (works today via cross-role default scoping, inconsistent); postgres_root is hardcoded to /srv/vault/{{ postgres_zone }}/pg rather than derived from luks_data_mount (a future mount-path change could desync the B2 preflight from where data actually lives, but verify.yml catches it post-apply); no regression test exercises the new B3/B4 guards WITHOUT #11 merged first — that's exactly what #11 fixes, hence the dependency. Also: POSTGRES_HOST_AUTH_METHOD=trust is set but inert today (overridden by explicit hba_file + read-only mount, caught by verify.yml if that changes); podman exec into the Postgres container as the platform-zone user grants Postgres superuser on the ledger, which is intentional (how migrations apply) — real trust boundary is the off-host daily anchor. SEQUENCE: this entry must merge AFTER #11 (dependsOn enforces this) so #11 lands into this PR's branch first, then this merge carries both changesets into main as the single top-branch→main landing per the stacked-PR convention.
